items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: He says, 'No, I want you to stay and conduct the show.'

ctx.x: and I put on a tuxedo and went in there and conducted the show, because everybody was so disgusted with the -- we never did get through a dress rehearsal that day. They never did get through a dress rehearsal, so I had to -- so we ran that show down, and when they ended the show, the audience was standing up screaming.

So now I go to Murray. I says, 'well, the show's on. I can go back to New York.' He says, 'No, I want you to stay and conduct the show.' So I stayed there and conducted the show, and this show was a big hit. I mean everybody -- so now Murray Wanger wanted to -- it was so big that he had a place next door in a much more fabulous building he wanted to put this show in. So he started getting this building ready to put this show in and move. And he told me.

And so he called me and said, look, he said. 'You did me a great favor,' he says. 'I'm going to make you rich.' He says, 'All you got to do now, stick with me,' and this guy never went to bed. You go up to his room, and he had six or seven telephones all around his bed. He never went to sleep -- calling, he had things in South America, everywhere. He was book -- he was really wild, and then he was renovating this building, had a building next door and had big display windows of fur coats and manniquins and…
